title_jp: おじいちゃんの{子ども|こども}の{頃|ころ}
context: Wednesday 2 December: {恵子|けいこ}さん gets a photo from {由美|ゆみ} of {颯太|そうた}'s school essay about his grandpa's childhood, and reads it with アルちゃん at the kotatsu while {田中|たなか}さん pretends not to listen.
scene: Wednesday night at the kotatsu. {恵子|けいこ}さん shows you {颯太|そうた}'s school essay. It's about {田中|たなか}さん as a boy.

phrases.jp: {子ども|こども}の{頃|ころ|time, days (when)|4}、よく{雪|ゆき}で{遊んだ|あそんだ}なあ。
phrases.en: When I was a kid, I often played in the snow.
phrases.note: なあ at the end: thinking aloud, a bit nostalgic.

phrases.jp: {去年|きょねん}に{比べて|くらべて}、{今年|ことし}は{雪|ゆき}が{多い|おおい}ね。
phrases.en: Compared to last year, there's more snow this year.
phrases.note: Perfect small talk in a snowy town.

phrases.jp: こっちの{生活|せいかつ|life, daily living|4}にも、だいぶ{慣れて|なれて|to get used to|4}きた。
phrases.en: I've got quite used to life here.
phrases.note: 〜てきた: a change that has been happening little by little.

phrases.jp: {将来|しょうらい|future|4}の{夢|ゆめ}は{何|なん}ですか。
phrases.en: What's your dream for the future?
phrases.note: The classic question every Japanese kid gets from adults.

phrases.jp: {家族|かぞく}の{昔|むかし}の{話|はなし}を{聞いて|きいて}、{驚きました|おどろきました|to be surprised|4}。
phrases.en: I was surprised to hear my family's old stories.
phrases.note: Reason in て-form + {驚|おどろ}く.

dialogue_setting: A photo of {颯太|そうた}'s essay on {恵子|けいこ}さん's phone, sent by {由美|ゆみ}: pencil on squared paper, with a red {花丸|はなまる} at the top.
text_title: おじいちゃんの{子ども|こども}の{頃|ころ|time, days (when)|4}　5{年|ねん}　{颯太|そうた}

dialogue.speaker: Homework
dialogue.jp: {社会|しゃかい}の{作文|さくぶん|essay, composition|3}の{宿題|しゅくだい}で、おじいちゃんに{子ども|こども}の{頃|ころ|time, days (when)|4}の{話|はなし}を{聞いた|きいた}。
dialogue.en: For my social studies essay homework, I asked Grandpa about when he was a kid.

dialogue.speaker: Snow
dialogue.jp: おじいちゃんが{子ども|こども}の{頃|ころ|time, days (when)|4}は、{今|いま}に{比べて|くらべて}{雪|ゆき}がずっと{多くて|おおくて}、{屋根|やね|roof|3}まで{積もった|つもった|to pile up (snow)|3}そうだ。
dialogue.en: When Grandpa was a kid, there was much more snow compared to now: it piled up to the roof, he says.

dialogue.speaker: Winter
dialogue.jp: {家|いえ}に{暖房|だんぼう|heating|3}はなくて、{兄弟|きょうだい|brothers and sisters|4}5{人|にん}で{一つ|ひとつ}のこたつに{入った|はいった}らしい。{驚いた|おどろいた|to be surprised|4}！
dialogue.en: The house had no heating, and five brothers and sisters squeezed under one kotatsu. I was amazed!

dialogue.speaker: Play
dialogue.jp: ゲームもなかった。でも{雪|ゆき}の{日|ひ}は、{ひいおじいちゃん||great-grandfather|3}がスキーに{連れて|つれて|to take (someone) along|4}{行って|いって}くれたそうだ。
dialogue.en: There were no video games either. But on snowy days, his dad (my great-grandpa) took him skiing.

dialogue.speaker: Today
dialogue.jp: {昔|むかし}に{比べて|くらべて}、{今|いま}の{生活|せいかつ|life, daily living|4}はずっと{便利|べんり}だ。でもおじいちゃんは「{不便|ふべん|inconvenient|3}だったけど、{楽しかった|たのしかった}」と{言った|いった}。
dialogue.en: Compared to the old days, life now is much more convenient. But Grandpa said, 'It was inconvenient, but it was fun.'

dialogue.speaker: My dream
dialogue.jp: {僕|ぼく}の{将来|しょうらい|future|4}の{夢|ゆめ}はサッカー{選手|せんしゅ|player (sports)|3}。でもいつか、おじいちゃんのりんご{畑|ばたけ|field, orchard|3}を{継ぎたい|つぎたい|to take over (a family business)|2}。
dialogue.en: My dream for the future is to be a footballer. But one day I want to take over Grandpa's apple orchard.

listening.intro: After school, {颯太|そうた} left a message on the house phone.

lines.jp: ばあちゃん、{僕|ぼく}！{作文|さくぶん|essay|3}、{先生|せんせい}に{花丸|はなまる|top mark (flower circle)|3}もらった！{土曜日|どようび}、じいちゃんに{見せる|みせる}ね。
lines.en: Grandma, it's me! I got a top mark from my teacher for my essay! I'll show it to Grandpa on Saturday.

listening.question: {颯太|そうた}は{土曜日|どようび}に{何|なに}をしますか。
options: おじいちゃんにさくぶんを見せる
せんせいにさくぶんを出す
おじいちゃんとスキーに行く
listening.explain: He says じいちゃんに{見|み}せるね: he'll show Grandpa the essay on Saturday.

grammar.form: noun + に{比|くら}べて ({昔|むかし}に{比|くら}べて, {去年|きょねん}に{比|くら}べて) · softer: noun + に{比|くら}べると ({東京|とうきょう}に{比|くら}べると) · two things: AとBを{比|くら}べると ({兄|あに}と{弟|おとうと}を{比|くら}べると)
grammar.explanation: Sets a reference point: 'compared to A, B is…'. It's used for a difference in degree, often with ずっと. The point takes に, never を: {昔|むかし}に{比|くら}べて, not {昔|むかし}を{比|くら}べて. AとBを{比|くら}べると is the separate way to put two things side by side.

examples.jp: {東京|とうきょう}に{比べて|くらべて}、ここは{家賃|やちん|rent|3}が{安い|やすい}。
examples.en: Compared to Tokyo, rent here is cheap.

examples.jp: {先月|せんげつ}に{比べると|くらべると}、{日本語|にほんご}がかなり{上手|じょうず}になった。
examples.en: Compared to last month, my Japanese has got a lot better.

quiz.question: {東京|とうきょう}＿＿、{鷹ノ原|たかのはら}は{星|ほし}がよく{見える|みえる}。
quiz.en: Compared to Tokyo, you can see the stars well in {鷹ノ原|たかのはら}.
quiz.explain: The reference point takes に: {東京|とうきょう}に{比|くら}べて.

quiz_more.question: {兄|あに}と{弟|おとうと}＿＿、{弟|おとうと}のほうが{背|せ}が{高い|たかい}。
quiz_more.en: If you compare my big brother and little brother, the little one is taller.
quiz_more.explain: Two things side by side: AとBを{比|くら}べると.

quiz_more.question: {十年前|じゅうねんまえ}に＿＿、{町|まち}の{人口|じんこう|population|3}は{減った|へった|to decrease|3}。
quiz_more.en: Compared to ten years ago, the town's population has gone down.
quiz_more.explain: Linking to the rest of the sentence needs the て-form: に{比|くら}べて.

kanji.where: In red pen at the top of {颯太|そうた}'s essay, next to the teacher's comment.
kanji.breakdown: {花丸|はなまる}: 花 flower + 丸 circle → a circle with petals drawn round it: 'excellent'.
kanji.related: {丸|まる} alone = correct. Teachers also stamp よくできました ('very well done').

tip.title: ○ is right, ✓ can be wrong
tip.body: In Japan a circle (○, まる) means correct and × (バツ) means wrong. A tick ✓ often marks a mistake, so don't panic if a form comes back full of them. マルをつける = to mark something as right.

challenge.prompt: {颯太|そうた} on the family LINE: 「アルちゃんの{町|まち}は？{子ども|こども}の{頃|ころ|time, days (when)|4}と{比べて|くらべて}どう？」 Tell him your town in Spain has got much bigger since you were a kid.

options.jp: {子|こ}どもの{頃|ころ}に{比|くら}べて、{町|まち}がずっと{大|おお}きくなったよ！
options.why: Reference point + に{比|くら}べて, past なった for a change that happened, casual for a kid.

options.jp: {子|こ}どもの{頃|ころ}を{比|くら}べて、{町|まち}がずっと{大|おお}きくなったよ！
options.why: The reference point takes に, not を.

options.jp: {子|こ}どもの{頃|ころ}より{比|くら}べて、{町|まち}がずっと{大|おお}きくなったよ！
options.why: Use より alone or に{比|くら}べて, not both together.

options.jp: {子|こ}どもの{頃|ころ}に{比|くら}べて、{町|まち}がずっと{大|おお}きくなるよ！
options.why: The change already happened: なった, not なる.

challenge.model_answer: {子ども|こども}の{頃|ころ|time, days (when)|4}に{比べて|くらべて}、{町|まち}がずっと{大きく|おおきく}なったよ！
challenge.explanation: {子|こ}どもの{頃|ころ}に{比|くら}べて sets the reference point, and ずっと stresses how big the difference is. {大|おお}きくなった is past because the town has already grown. Plain form + よ is right for chatting with an 11-year-old.
challenge.hint: reference point + に{比|くら}べて

vocab.note: {作|さく} make + {文|ぶん} sentences. The school kind; a university essay is レポート.
{子|こ}どもの{頃|ころ} = as a kid. 3{時|じ}{頃|ごろ} = about 3 o'clock (read ごろ).
In snow country people climb up to clear it: {屋根|やね}の{雪下|ゆきお}ろし.
{暖|だん} warm + {房|ぼう} room. Opposite: {冷房|れいぼう}, air conditioning.
{兄|きょう} older + {弟|だい} younger brother. Often used for sisters too.
Written style; in speech people often say びっくりした.
Everyday life: {田舎|いなか}の{生活|せいかつ}. Not 'a life story' ({人生|じんせい}).
{不|ふ} not + {便利|べんり} convenient. A な-adjective.
Your own future plans: {将来|しょうらい}の{夢|ゆめ}. {未来|みらい} is the future in general.
A family business or farm: {店|みせ}を{継|つ}ぐ, {家|いえ}を{継|つ}ぐ.

kanji_study.kun: あたた(かい)・あたた(める)
kanji_study.parts: 日 sun radical + 爰 a hand reaching out → the sun's warmth reaching you: warm.
kanji_study.lookalike: Not 温 (warm, of water and things): 温 has 氵 water; 暖 has 日 sun, for air and weather.

kanji_study.meaning: take along, link, in a row
kanji_study.parts: 車 cart + 辶 road radical → carts travelling the road one after another: in a row, take along.
kanji_study.lookalike: Not 運 (carry): 運 has 軍 army inside 辶; 連 has just 車.

words.en: long weekend, run of days off

extras.title: Winter life in the old days
extras.title_jp: {昔|むかし}の{冬|ふゆ}の{暮らし|くらし}
extras.intro: Things {田中|たなか}さん's generation grew up with.

items.note: A fire pit in the floor, for cooking and heat.
Still sold today; many people take one to bed.
Worn at home over your clothes.
Kids helped every morning; still a daily job here.

extras.title: Family words: mine and yours
extras.title_jp: {家族|かぞく}の{呼び方|よびかた}
extras.intro: Your own family (humble word) and someone else's (polite word).

items.note: {祖母|そぼ} for your own, おばあさん for someone else's.

items.jp: {両親|りょうしん|parents|4}／ご{両親|りょうしん}
items.note: Add ご for someone else's parents.
{孫|まご} grandchild + ひ. Same ひ as in ひいおじいちゃん.
One word for every cousin, male or female.
